feedback: Approving this candidate as the first real test of the off-track diagnosis. Its evidence base is iteration 0 only: all 60 trials went off track after about 2 line-loss events, with max_error near 0.06 m (the 0.0625 m limit) and rms_error about 0.025 to 0.029 m. That points to overshoot and loss of the line on bends. This candidate changes only the controller (kp 4.0 to 2.5, kd 0.1 to 0.3, base_speed 1.8 to 1.6) and keeps the geometry fixed, so the race isolates the gain change. Nothing here predicts its outcome. Weigh the next telemetry this way. If line_loss_events fall and runs stay on track with progress well above 0.13, keep kp near 2.5 and raise base_speed toward 2.0 to recover the time budget, since 1.6 may not reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. If runs still leave the track with line_loss_events still near 2, the cause is more likely sensor geometry or the line-loss response than gain, so test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' before more gain changes. If steering_oscillation stays high, lower kp further or raise kd.
requested_changes: If the runs stay on track (line_loss_events 0 or 1) but do not finish within 3.0 s: raise controller.base_speed from 1.6 toward 2.0, keeping kp 2.5 and kd 0.3, since iteration 0 showed speed was not the limit for leaving the track.

If runs still leave the track with line_loss_events near 2 and max_error near 0.06: keep the gains and change controller.line_loss from 'last_direction' to 'search_left' or 'search_right' to test the line-loss response.
If steering_oscillation stays above about 0.15 while the robot stays on track: lower controller.kp from 2.5 toward 1.8 or raise controller.kd from 0.3 toward 0.5.
